name: @rolling-design-sync/mcp

tools.name: list_files
tools.description:
List tracked files

Every file the plugin has synced, most recently synced first, with node counts (total, dirty, clean, blocked) and the last sync time. Use it to find a `fileKey` when you have no Figma link; with a link, pass it as `url` (or use `resolve_url`).

tools.name: get_file
tools.description:
Get a file

One tracked file's node counts and last sync time: a quick check of how much is dirty. For counts by category, type or frame use `summarize`. `file_not_found`: the file was never synced — take the key from `list_files`, or pass the Figma link as `url` with fileKey '-'.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

tools.name: update_file_settings
tools.description:
Change file settings

Changes a tracked file's settings; returns the file with every setting (defaults filled in). Agent tokens and agent portal sessions only (viewers get wrong_token_class). `trackLibraryComponents` (default true): false stops tracking library (remote) components — the plugin stops scanning library mains at its next sync, and stored library nodes drop out of listings, summaries, counts, work-item progress and trends (nothing is deleted; true restores them). Instances of library components stay tracked; with `expand=instances` their mains appear as `kind: "library"` reference items. Unknown settings are invalid_parameter. Emits `file.settings_changed` (`data.settings`) when a setting changes; its actor is the body's `worker` when given, `portal:<label>` on a session-authenticated call, else the token label.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

settings.description: The settings to change (trackLibraryComponents); others keep their value.

trackLibraryComponents.description: Default true. false: library (remote) components are not tracked — the plugin does not scan or upload library mains, and stored library nodes are left out of listings, summaries, counts, work-item progress and trends (not deleted; `library=include` still lists them). Instances of library components stay tracked.

worker.description: Your worker id; recorded as the event actor (default: the token label).

tools.name: list_scopes
tools.description:
List synced scopes

The scopes (sections/frames) the plugin has synced in a file: each root's name, last sync, and current counts. Only nodes under these roots exist in the API; a `node_not_found` usually means the node is outside every scope and must be synced from the plugin first.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description:
List nodes

Nodes of a file with their property-level changes — by default the dirty ones (design changed since last built), compact, in document order (the design's layer order), 100 per page. The main read for implementation work: filter by subtree (`under` — one node id or several comma-separated — or a `url` with node-id), type, change, category, component or name; values within a parameter are OR, parameters are AND. Each node's `changes` is `{ prop: { built, now } }` and `contentHash` is what `clear_nodes` needs. For counts only use `summarize`; to work component by component use `list_work_items`. Every node carries `changedProps` and, for instances, `isInstance` / `mainComponentId` (`instance=true` lists only instances). By default (`changes=auto`) `added` nodes have no `changes` — on a fresh sync every node is added, so pages stay small; get their values with `changes=diff`, `view=full` or `get_node`. Change values over 1 KB are replaced by `{ truncated: true, bytes }` and the page has `truncated: true`; `view=full` or `get_node` returns them whole. `expand=instances` returns everything a screen uses in one call: with `under` = the screen, it adds the main components its instances point at (and theirs, transitively), each once; filters apply to that union (`expand=instances&state=dirty` = every dirty node the screen uses). Scope nodes come first, then each component in discovery order; expanded nodes carry `via` (the instance that reached them), and `expansion` reports the count, `truncated` and `unresolved` (unsynced) components. Page with `nextCursor` → `cursor`. On `unknown_parameter` / `invalid_parameter` follow `hint`; on `invalid_cursor` keep every other parameter unchanged or drop `cursor`.

state.description: Comma-separated: dirty, clean, blocked, requested, all. Default dirty (changed since last built or with open notes, not blocked); `requested`: dirty only by open notes; `all` for every state.

under.description: Only this node's subtree, the node included (1:2 or 1-2). Several subtrees: up to 50 comma-separated ids (1:2,1:5) for their union, each node once, in the order given. Defaults to the `url` link's node-id.

depth.description: Needs `under`: at most this many levels below it — below each root when there are several (1 = direct children).

type.description: Comma-separated Figma node types, e.g. TEXT,INSTANCE,FRAME.

changeType.description: Comma-separated: added, modified, deleted, requested (dirty nodes only; `requested`: built as designed but with open notes).

hasNotes.description: true: only nodes with open notes; false: only nodes without.

changed.description: Comma-separated changed property names (fills, paddingLeft); a trailing `*` matches a prefix (padding*).

category.description: Comma-separated change categories: layout, color, typography, effects, component, content, structure, prototype, token, other, note.

component.description: Comma-separated main component ids: the components and all their instances.

name.description: Comma-separated case-insensitive name globs (`*`, `?`), e.g. Button*.

since.description: ISO 8601 time: only nodes changed at or after it.

instance.description: true: only component instances (`isInstance`); false: only other nodes.

library.description: Library nodes (remote main components / sets and their layers): include, exclude, or only them. Default: include when the file tracks library components (`settings.trackLibraryComponents`), else exclude.

q.description: All the filters above in one string: space-separated `key:value` pairs, e.g. `state:dirty under:1:2 changed:fills` (several subtrees: `under:1:2,1:5`); quote values with spaces (name:"Primary Button"). A key may not also be passed as its own parameter.

view.description: compact (default: state, changes, hash, claim, block) or full (adds attrs, implementedAttrs, path; change values never truncated).

changes.description: auto (default): the built→now diff for modified and deleted nodes, omitted for added ones (their property names are in `changedProps`) — keeps fresh-sync pages small; diff: the diff for every node, including added ones' full values; names: never `changes`, only `changedProps`. Ask for `changes=diff` (or `get_node`) when you need the values of added nodes.

fields.description: Comma-separated node fields to return (overrides view): nodeId, name, type, parentId, isInstance, mainComponentId, component, state, changeType, changedProps, changes, changesKnown, contentHash, figmaUrl, library, claim, blocked, notes, attrs, implementedAttrs, path, deleted, notesResolved, history, descendants, usage, via (`via` needs `expand=instances`).

include.description: Comma-separated: counts, usage. `counts` adds subtree counts (`descendants`) to each node; `usage` adds `usage: { layers }` to each design token (`token:<variableKey>`).

sort.description: document (default: the design's layer order — auto-layout flow order, else top-to-bottom, left-to-right), path (node-id path order), updatedAt or name; prefix `-` for descending.

limit.description: Page size (default 100, max 1000). With format=outline: rendered lines per page (default: every line).

cursor.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`, unchanged, with all other parameters the same (else `invalid_cursor`). With format=outline: the previous response's `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header (a line position in the rendered outline).

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

expand.description: `instances`: also include the subtree of every main component the scope's instances use (the scope is `under`, or the whole file) — transitively through instances inside those components, breadth-first, each component once. Use it for "everything this screen uses" / "which components do I build for this screen". Other filters apply after expansion; `depth` cannot be combined with it.

expandDepth.description: With `expand=instances`: at most this many instance → main hops (default 10, max 20; 1 = only the components the scope uses directly).

format.description: json (default); ndjson — one JSON object per line, streamed; md — a markdown checklist, one line per row, streamed. ndjson and md return every match from `cursor` on (up to `limit` when given) instead of one page. outline — text/plain, an indented tree with one line per node: use this first to see a screen's structure (under=<the screen>, and expand=instances for the components inside). Line: `Name (TYPE) · added` — `clean`, `added`, `deleted`, or `modified (3: fills, paddingLeft, …)` (changed property count and the first names), `· blocked` when blocked; an instance shows `(INSTANCE → <mainComponentId> <main name>)`. Two spaces per level of the tree below `under` (the `under` node itself, when it matches, is at the left margin; with several `under` ids, the tree of each root follows that of the previous root, in the order given, each root at the left margin). A node whose ancestors the filters leave out is indented under its nearest shown ancestor (at the margin when none is shown) — no placeholder lines. With expand=instances, a component's subtree is nested, as `↳ Name (COMPONENT) · …`, under the first instance that reached it; other instances of it show `→ <mainComponentId> (shown above)` (or `(shown below)`). Always in document order (the design's layer order; `sort=path` for node-id path order); nodes positioned absolutely in an auto-layout parent are marked `(absolute)`. Lines are the `fields`-independent summary. The whole result (up to 2000 rows, in order) is rendered once, then paged by rendered lines, so nesting and `(shown above)` read the same at any page size: `limit` is lines per page (default: every line), and when lines remain the response has an `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header — pass it as `cursor`, with every other parameter unchanged, for the next lines. Past the 2000-row cap the outline's last line (counted like any other) is `… N more (use cursor/limit) — cursor=<c>` (the same cursor is in the header), which continues after the rendered part.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

tools.name: get_node
tools.description:
Get a node

One node in full: state, property changes (whole values, never truncated), component link (`isInstance`, `mainComponentId`), current `contentHash`, claim, block, subtree counts and history (when and in which commit it was last built). Use it to re-read a node before clearing it — e.g. after `clear_nodes` reports it `stale`. `node_not_found`: check the id against the link's node-id and that it is under a synced scope (`list_scopes`).

changes.description: diff (default): the whole built→now diff, never truncated — the way to read an added node's values; auto: omitted for added nodes; names: never `changes`, only `changedProps`.

tools.name: resolve_url
tools.description:
Resolve a Figma link

Turns a Figma link into `{ fileKey, nodeId }` (nodeId as 1:2; `null` when the link has no node-id). Needs no tracked file. Most calls also take the link directly as `url` with '-' path parameters, so use this only when you need the ids themselves. `invalid_url`: pass a figma.com/design/… link, URL-encoded.

tools.name: list_claims
tools.description:
List file claims

Active (unexpired) claims, soonest expiry first. `nodeCount` counts nodes still leased to each claim; `nodeIds` contains at most 500 of them in node-id order; `nodes` names the first 3 in document order. Cleared, released, expired or reassigned nodes are excluded. Use this to see agents at work, then list_nodes with claimed=mine and worker to inspect a worker's nodes.

tools.name: claim_nodes
tools.description:
Claim nodes

Leases nodes to `worker` so parallel agents do not implement the same nodes. Claim before working when other agents may share the file; alone, you can skip claims. Select by `nodeIds` or by `filter` (not both; neither = the dirty nodes, up to `limit`). Only free, expired or already-yours nodes are taken, and the response lists exactly those — work on those only; an empty `nodes` means nothing free matched. The lease ends at `expiresAt`: `renew_claim` before then for long work; `clear_nodes` releases cleared nodes, `release_claim` the rest.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

worker.description: A stable id for your agent session; reuse it on every call.

label.description: A short human-readable name for the work, shown in logs and UIs.

ttlSeconds.description: Lease length in seconds (default: the server's RDS_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS; capped at 86400 = 24 h).

limit.description: At most this many nodes (default 100 with a filter; every listed id with nodeIds).

nodeIds.description: Exact node ids to claim (1:2 or 1-2); unknown ids are skipped.

filter.description: The `list_nodes` filters (`q` included) selecting the nodes to claim, e.g. `{ "under": "1:2", "category": "color" }` (`under` may list several roots: `"1:2,1:5"`); `claimed` and `worker` are implied. `{}` = the dirty nodes.

under.description: Only this node's subtree, the node included (1:2 or 1-2). Several subtrees: up to 50 comma-separated ids (1:2,1:5) for their union, each node once, in the order given. Defaults to the `url` link's node-id.

tools.name: clear_nodes
tools.description:
Clear implemented nodes

Records nodes as implemented (up to 500 per call) once your code matches the design: they become clean, their current design becomes the new baseline, and their leases are released. Send each node with the `contentHash` you implemented (from `list_nodes` / `get_node`). Each item is checked on its own and the call is 200 even when some fail: `cleared`; `stale` — the design changed since you read it, so re-read that node with `get_node`, implement the new changes and clear it with the returned `contentHash`; `not_found` — a wrong id; `not_removed` — `subtree: true` on a node that is not deleted (nothing cleared). Removed design (a `kind: "removed"` work item): once its code is gone, clear just its root with `subtree: true` — that also clears every dirty deleted node below it (`subtreeCleared`); live nodes below are untouched. Clear only what you actually built; never clear to hide changes (use `block_node` for nodes you cannot implement). The `nodes.cleared` event's actor is the body's `worker` when given, `portal:<label>` on a session-authenticated call, else the token label.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

commitRef.description: The commit (SHA or ref) that implements the nodes; shown in node history.

worker.description: Your worker id; recorded as the `nodes.cleared` actor (default: the token label).

items.description: The nodes to clear (1–500), each with the `contentHash` you implemented.

contentHash.description: The node's `contentHash` as you read it before implementing.

subtree.description: For a deleted (removed) root: also clear every dirty deleted node below it. On a live node the item fails with `not_removed`.

tools.name: renew_claim
tools.description:
Renew a claim

Extends the lease (to now + `ttlSeconds`) on the nodes still held under this claim; nodes cleared, released, expired or re-claimed since are not renewed, and the response lists the rest. Renew before `expiresAt` while work takes longer than the lease. `claim_not_found`: the id is wrong — take a new claim with `claim_nodes`.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

ttlSeconds.description: Lease length in seconds (default: the server's RDS_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS; capped at 86400 = 24 h).

tools.name: release_claim
tools.description:
Release a claim

Ends the claim and frees the nodes still under it, so other agents can take them. Call it when you stop without clearing everything (cleared nodes are already released). `claim_not_found`: the id is wrong; an unreleased lease simply expires at `expiresAt`.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description:
List file events

The file's activity log, oldest first: syncs, clears, claims, blocks (IDs, counts and labels, never design content). Use it to see what changed since you last looked, or who holds what. JSON page `{ events, nextAfter }`: poll with `after` = the previous `nextAfter`; `after=0` starts from the oldest retained event. After a `sync.completed`, re-read the affected nodes. To read the newest events first, pass `order=desc`: the page `{ events, nextBefore }` is newest first; pass `before` = the previous `nextBefore` for the next older page (omit `before` to start at the newest event). A page shorter than `limit` is the last one. Filters apply the same in both orders. Types: sync.completed, nodes.cleared, claim.created, claim.renewed, claim.released, node.blocked, node.unblocked, file.settings_changed, note.added, note.resolved, note.dismissed. With `Accept: text/event-stream`: a server-sent-event stream. Each message has `id` (the event id), `event` (the type) and `data` (the event as JSON). It replays the events after `Last-Event-ID` (header, sent by EventSource on reconnect) or `?after=`, then streams live; without either it streams live only. A `: heartbeat` comment is sent every 20 s. When the requested id is older than the replay window (RDS_EVENT_REPLAY_HOURS), one `event: reset` is sent instead of the replay — re-fetch state — and the stream continues live. `format` applies to the JSON page only (`ndjson` / `md` stream every event after `after` — with order=desc, before `before`, newest first — up to `limit` when given). `nodeId` matches data.nodeId or a member of data.nodeIds in JSON and SSE. `since` is an inclusive ISO timestamp lower bound on JSON pages (ignored for SSE). Filters combine with types, after and before. `order` and `before` apply to JSON pages only (SSE is always oldest first).

after.description: Only events with a greater id: the previous page's `nextAfter` (default 0 = from the start of the log).

before.description: Only events with a smaller id: with order=desc, the previous page's `nextBefore` (default: from the newest event). JSON pages only.

order.description: `asc` (default): oldest first, page with `after` / `nextAfter`. `desc`: newest first, page with `before` / `nextBefore`. JSON pages only; SSE is unchanged.

types.description: Comma-separated event types: sync.completed, nodes.cleared, claim.created, claim.renewed, claim.released, node.blocked, node.unblocked, file.settings_changed, note.added, note.resolved, note.dismissed.

url.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

nodeId.description: Only events mentioning this node in data.nodeId or data.nodeIds (1:2 or 1-2); JSON and SSE.

since.description: Inclusive ISO timestamp lower bound on createdAt for JSON pages; ignored for SSE.

format.description: json (default); ndjson — one JSON object per line, streamed; md — a markdown checklist, one line per row, streamed. ndjson and md return every match from `cursor` on (up to `limit` when given) instead of one page.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

tools.name: block_node
tools.description:
Block a node

Marks a node you cannot implement (missing asset, unclear or impossible design, needs a human) as blocked, with a reason (1–500 chars) a person can act on. It leaves the default dirty listing (list it with `state=blocked`) until `unblock_node` or its next design change, and its lease is released. Blocking a blocked node replaces the reason. Use it instead of clearing a node you did not build.

Unblock a node

Removes a node's block once its blocker is resolved: it is dirty again (back in the default listing) or clean, by its hashes. `unblocked: false` when it was not blocked — nothing changed. A design change unblocks a node on its own.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description:
Add a note to a node

Records that the built node does not match the design, with what is wrong. An open note makes the node dirty — `changeType: requested` (category `note`) when its design is otherwise built, or its design change plus category `note` — and keeps it dirty across re-syncs. The node is listed with its open `notes` until it is cleared (`clear_nodes` resolves its notes) or the note is dismissed. Viewer tokens and sessions may add notes too. Returns the note and the node's new state; a tombstoned node cannot take notes.

body.description: What does not match the design, as a person would say it (1–4000 chars).

worker.description: Your worker id, recorded on the note.

annotations.title: Add a note to a node

tools.name: dismiss_note
tools.description:
Dismiss a note

Closes an open note without changing the build (e.g. it is wrong or already handled); the node's state is recomputed without it. Its author or any agent may dismiss it. To resolve a note by fixing the code, clear the node instead.

tools.name: summarize
tools.description:
Summarize changes

Counts of the nodes the `list_nodes` filters match (default: dirty) by state, change type, change category and node type — a cheap overview before listing or planning work. With one `under` (e.g. a page), `byFrame` also counts per child frame of it (not with several `under` ids). With `expand=instances` the counts cover everything the scope uses — its nodes plus the main components its instances reach, transitively (`byFrame` still counts only nodes under `under`): how big is this screen, components included? Returns no nodes; use `list_nodes` or `list_work_items` for those.

tools.name: get_trends
tools.description:
Weekly trends

How fast the backlog moves: nodes cleared and nodes newly dirtied by syncs in the last `windowDays` days (default 7) and the change in clears vs the window before, for the whole server (`total`) and each tracked file (`files`); `fileKey` narrows both to one file. Counts come from the event log, so `complete` is false when RDS_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS (`retentionDays`) keeps less than two windows — `clearedPrevious` and `clearedChangePct` may then undercount. Returns no nodes.

tools.name: list_work_items
tools.description:
List work items

The nodes the `list_nodes` filters match (default: dirty) bundled into work items — the best way to plan: fix a component once and its instances follow. Items are in document order (the design's layer order, by each item's key node), paged by `cursor`; each has its node ids (`claim_nodes` takes them), changed properties and categories. `group=component` (default): by the nearest COMPONENT / COMPONENT_SET ancestor-or-self; nodes with none form one item with `key: null`, listed last. Removed design (group=component and group=set): deleted nodes that were built are grouped under their removed root — the topmost deleted node — into one `kind: "removed"` item (after the component items, before `key: null`, in the roots' document order), unless that root sits inside a live component (then they are part of that component's item). For a removed item: remove the code that rendered the root; keep components in `uses` with `livePlacements > 0` (still used elsewhere), consider removing those with 0; heed `warnings`; then clear the root with `subtree: true` (`clear_nodes`) — one item clears the whole removed subtree. Deleted nodes that were never built are not work (they resolve at sync). Design tokens (group=component and group=set): the dirty tokens of each collection form one `kind: "tokens"` item (key = the collection node id, after the component and removed items, before `key: null`). For each token, update the code variable named by its `codeSyntax` (WEB, else the token name) for every changed `value:<Mode>`, then clear it. `include=usage` adds how many layers use each token. `group=set`: merge variants of each known component set into one item named like the Figma set, with its Figma key, set reference and variants [{ key, name, nodeCount }]. Use this to build a design system. Standalone components and variants whose set is unavailable keep their component item; the default grouping is unchanged. `group=frame`: by the ancestor one level below `under` (required); the `under` node itself is in the `key: null` item. `include=progress` adds { total, clean } for each returned item across all states, independent of state= and the nodeIds cap. Use clean / total for a progress bar. `expand=instances` answers "which components do I need to build for this screen, and how often does it use each?": with `under` = the screen, items also cover every main component its instances reach (transitively, each once; filters apply after expansion), and with `group=component` each item has `placementsInScope` beside the file-wide `placements`. Nodes of expanded components that are outside `under` fall in the `key: null` item with `group=frame`. Notes: a node someone noted as not matching the design is dirty with `changeType: requested` (category `note`) when its design is otherwise built, and grouped like any dirty node; `notes` counts an item's open notes. Read the notes (`get_node` or `list_notes`), fix the code to match the design as they describe, then clear the node — clearing resolves its notes. Each item's `changes` maps its listed node ids to their diffs (`changes=auto`: modified and deleted nodes; `diff`: added ones too; `names`: none — `changedProps` only). Values over 1 KB are `{ truncated: true, bytes }` and the page has `truncated: true`; `get_node` returns them whole.

Each item is a line `Name (TYPE) · 3 nodes · changed (4: characters, fills, …) · 2 placements`, with its listed nodes as an indented tree below it (`Name (TYPE) · modified (…)`, indented under their nearest listed ancestor). Lines are the `fields`-independent summary. The whole result (up to 2000 lines of whole items, in order) is rendered once, then paged by rendered lines, so nesting and `(shown above)` read the same at any page size: `limit` is lines per page (default: every line), and when lines remain the response has an `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header — pass it as `cursor`, with every other parameter unchanged, for the next lines. instructions: rolling-design-sync tracks what changed in Figma since it was last built, node by node. The tools are generated from the connected API's OpenAPI document. Loop: (1) list_nodes for the screen or component you are working on (or claim_nodes to lease nodes when several agents share a file; summarize / list_work_items for an overview); (2) implement each node's `changes` — per property { built, now, category }, with token names where a value is bound — mapping it to code via Code Connect / figma.ts mappings where present, and pulling live details for that node only from the Figma MCP via its figmaUrl; (3) clear_nodes with the nodeId + contentHash pairs you read and the commit SHA. An item that comes back `stale` changed again after you read it: re-read that node with get_node, implement the newer change, and clear it with its new contentHash — never retry the old hash. Use block_node for a node you cannot implement instead of clearing it. Any tool that takes fileKey / nodeId also takes a Figma link as `url`; fileKey defaults to RDS_FILE_KEY when that is set in the server env. Listing tools return 25 results per call unless you pass limit (text formats: up to that many lines; format=outline: the whole outline unless you pass limit, in lines); a result that ends with `More results: call again with cursor="…"` has more — repeat the call with that cursor and every other input unchanged. Results too large for one reply come back as a smaller page. Where the connected API offers them (they then appear in the tool inputs): expand=instances follows instances into their main components, so one list_nodes / summarize / list_work_items call covers everything a screen uses; format=outline returns a screen as an indented text tree — the quickest answer to "what's in this screen" (with expand=instances for the components inside); changes=names lists only the changed property names (changedProps) and changes=diff every built → now value — use list_work_items with expand=instances and changes=names for "what do I build", then get_node for the values of one node.
